name: Fidelismo
summary: Fidelismo is the set of beliefs of Fidel Castro and the Cuban Revolution: Cuban nationalism and anti-imperialism that became Marxist-Leninist after 1959, with a vanguard party, a planned socialist economy and revolutionary internationalism. It holds that legal reform cannot dislodge entrenched ruling classes, that armed struggle is justified, and that moral incentives should replace material self-interest.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Fidelismo holds that armed struggle is justified and Cuba maintains revolutionary armed forces; abolition contradicts this.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: My Life, ch. 11 (The Conspiracies Begin): after the agrarian reform the remaining parcels were "legalize[d]" so campesinos held "ownership of the land that they already occupied"; only the largest estates, the sugar plantations, stayed as state enterprises, and he says Cuba did not carry out Soviet-style "forced collectivization".

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: My Life, ch. 14 (The Death of Che Guevara): asked whether Cuba helped the Salvadoran guerrillas, he answers that "we gave them some modest aid" and describes sending recovered American weapons to the FMLN; ch. 15 (Cuba and Africa) says Cuba prepared fighting units and sent instructors and material aid to the Angolan and Guinea-Bissau independence movements from 1965.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: My Life, ch. 26 (Cuba Today): he says Reagan wrongly called the ANC, Namibia's independence fighters, "the Palestinians fighting for their own independent state" and Salvadoran patriots "terrorists"; he adds that Cuba itself would never use methods that "sacrifice innocent people".

arms-reduction.rationale: UN speech (1960): "we wholeheartedly support" the Soviet proposal for "total and complete disarmament" and urges that a fifth of arms spending go to development.

bound-labor.rationale: Fidelismo is hostile to feudal landlordism and gave land to tenants and sharecroppers.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: a revolutionary party "leads and works basically through its mass organizations" (unions, youth, women's federations, defence committees), which he calls its instruments.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Second Declaration expects imperialism's crisis to provoke revolution.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Second Declaration of Havana (1962): the capitalist system's "rapacious wars" are named as part of the system, and competition between monopolistic nations over uneven industrial power is said to have produced "imperialist wars" costing "fifty million dead"; World War II is again blamed on the imperialist powers.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: he describes the rising bourgeoisie's system as "a significant step forward from the previous system" with "extraordinary development of technique, of production", before it becomes "an obstacle". The Second Declaration says that once feudal bonds were broken the productive forces developed extraordinarily, and that capitalism, "once it had given all of which it was capable", became an obstacle to humanity's progress.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: My Life, ch. 9 (Lessons from a Guerrilla War): "You can't kill innocent people", he says, and fighting the enemy's forces in combat is the only way to justify violence; he says his movement used neither terrorism nor assassinations.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Second Declaration rejects "civilising" pretexts: imperial motives were economic.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle is central and Castro called for a united party of workers, peasants and others against the old order.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist and the Second Declaration analyses history as class conflict from feudal society onward.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Castro insisted on one united revolutionary organisation and the Soviet-aligned view rejected class struggle after socialism.

collective-defense.rationale: My Life, ch. 13 (The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962): what he asked of the Soviets was a public statement that "an attack on Cuba will be considered an attack on the Soviet Union".

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana condemns colonial exploitation of dependent territories for the benefit of metropolitan powers.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Second Declaration condemns US monopolies' control; the constitution condemns imperialism.

death-penalty.rationale: My Life, ch. 18 (The Ochoa Case and the Death Penalty): he defends executions for the gravest crimes, says the laws remain although not applied, and that after a plane bombing Cuba "would not accept an amnesty" or pardon for the guilty.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Fidelismo is anti-imperialist and insists on sovereign equality of states against dominant powers; Second Declaration of Havana rejects submission to the US.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: My Life, ch. 28 (After Fidel, What?): he says multiparty systems with many parties are "madness" and electoral contests a popularity show, and that the Cuban people value "unity". He does not discuss opposing positions inside the party.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Castro cited Lenin's State and Revolution on smashing the old state machine and the party leads a socialist revolution.

direct-action.rationale: The movement came to power by armed action, and Castro argued reform through elections was impossible under oligarchic control.

dominated-front.rationale: The Second Declaration calls Latin America's peoples to unite against imperialism and Cuba allied with the Third World.

economic-freedom.rationale: Fidelismo holds that economic freedom for capital undermines national and social freedom.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Rio speech (1992): "An important biological species is in danger of disappearing": mankind. He urges that the destruction stop at once: "Tomorrow it will be too late to do what we should have done a long time ago."

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: My Life, ch. 18 (The Ochoa Case and the Death Penalty): he says Cuba defended itself "through laws, rules, legal procedures" and avoided "anything that might be extra-legal or extra-judicial"; drug-transport death sentences were passed by the National Assembly and applied after trial.

force-without-un.rationale: My Life, ch. 26 (Cuba Today): he says the US claim to decide alone whether to attack other nations, and its talk of "preventive war", violates "the spirit and letter of the United Nations charter", and asks that the UN and multilateralism be preserved.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: 1980 May Day speech asks the US to "respect Nicaragua, respect Grenada and do not interfere" and calls for "noninterference in the domestic affairs of other Latin American peoples"; My Life, ch. 14 (The Death of Che Guevara): "we observed international law ... revolution can't be exported". The First Declaration of Havana "energetically condemns the overt and criminal intervention" of the United States over the nations of Latin America.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: My Life, ch. 28 (After Fidel, What?): subsidies will be cut back, but "only essential, vital things will be subsidized or free", including medical and educational services.

free-trade.rationale: Fidelismo condemns imperialist exploitation through unequal trade of raw materials for costly manufactures.

gradual-change.rationale: The Second Declaration says legal reform is impossible and the duty of every revolutionary is to make revolution.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: Rio speech (1992): he says consumer societies have "saturated the atmosphere with gases which are changing weather conditions with a catastrophic effect" and are "fundamentally responsible for the brutal destruction of the environment".

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fidelismo holds that sovereignty requires transforming the property system against imperialist control.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: My Life, ch. 19 (Cuba and Neoliberal Globalization): "We have never considered the idea of fabricating nuclear weapons, because we don't need them"; he says no one should have the right to produce them.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fidelismo seeks industrialisation and blames imperialism, not industry, for poverty.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: On Czechoslovakia (1968) he says the socialist bloc "has the right to prevent" a member falling "into the arms of imperialism" and accepts "the bitter necessity" of sending troops, while admitting the act has "absolutely no legality"; he backs it on political, not legal, grounds.

land-redistribution.rationale: Castro's 1953 program gave land to tenants, sharecroppers and squatters.

leader-cult.rationale: My Life, ch. 17 (The Collapse of the Soviet Union) and ch. 26 (Cuba Today): he says Cuba banned naming streets, buildings or statues after living leaders and that he has "fought adamantly against any manifestation of the cult of personality".

limit-population.rationale: My Life, ch. 19 (Cuba and Neoliberal Globalization): he calls a world population growing by "almost 100 million people a year" a new danger and says "China has made heroic efforts to limit its population growth"; he ties the explosion to illiteracy and poverty rather than to coercion.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Moncada attackers and the revolution's dead are honoured as martyrs, and 'Patria o muerte' is a central cult.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism requires members to carry out party decisions.

national-self-determination.rationale: UN speech (1960): "We proclaim the right of people to freedom, the right of people to nationhood"; he backs Algerian independence "100 percent" and all remaining colonial peoples. The First Declaration of Havana condemns US intervention as "detrimental to the national self-determination" of the Latin American nations and proclaims "the right of nations to their full sovereignty".

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: "there are no middle roads between capitalism and socialism"; anyone seeking "some third positions" holds "a really false and really utopian position".

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: History Will Absolve Me and the Second Declaration justify armed struggle and violence against the tyranny and its backers.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana denounces US domination of Latin America, and demanding the end of the Guantanamo base is central to Castroism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: My Life, ch. 13 (The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962): when the Soviets proposed medium-range missiles he told them Cuba "agreed to the installation of as many medium-range rockets as might be necessary", after the National Directorate unanimously accepted.

no-transition-to-communism.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: the working class holds power "during the entire stage of the building of socialism"; in 1987 he calls socialism "a first and transitional stage to communism".

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: OLAS closing speech (1967): "We must do away with the differentiation between legal and illegal means; methods should be classified as revolutionary or non-revolutionary."

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: OLAS closing speech (1967): "those who believe that they are going to win against the imperialists in elections are just plain naive", since the ruling class runs the media and the repressive apparatus; a peaceful road is "a lie". The Second Declaration likewise calls it neither honorable nor correct to beguile people with the "fallacious and convenient illusion" of uprooting entrenched ruling classes by legal means.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Guadalajara summit interview (1991): Cuba's neighbourhood assemblies, not the Party, nominate candidates, and the system gives "a greater degree of popular participation than anywhere else"; My Life, ch. 28 (After Fidel, What?) repeats that "the people who live in each electoral district meet in an assembly and nominate".

patriarchy-structural.rationale: My Life, ch. 10: "our machismo was inherited ... in capitalist societies", with "prejudices, very strong ones" against women; the 1963 women's congress speech says woman is "exploited as a worker and discriminated against as a woman".

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The 1953 program targeted ill-gotten wealth of previous officials as a core grievance, applied to the pre-revolutionary elite.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: OLAS closing speech (1967): "in the long run, there is only one solution... guerrilla warfare in Latin America"; he calls armed struggle the means by which socialism wins power. The Gran Enciclopèdia Catalana's entry on Castrism, as read here, treats armed popular revolution as the doctrine's means.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Second Declaration blames imperialist exploitation for Latin American poverty.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1953 program prioritised peasants, workers and the unemployed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The movement adopted Marxism-Leninism, whose core holds that profit comes from exploiting labour, and the Second Declaration of Havana denounces capitalist and imperialist exploitation.

proportional-representation.rationale: My Life, ch. 28 (After Fidel, What?): he criticises party-list systems where the party leader "decided who would make up the parliament" and voters "the voter votes for that abstract thing", and says the single-member constituency method "is a little bit better".

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Second Declaration frames politics by class and anti-imperialist struggle, not racial group interests.

rent-control.rationale: Castro's 1953 defence speech gives the revolutionary government's housing plan: "cutting all rents in half" by law, with landlords' threat to freeze building named as the problem the State must override.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Castro justified the revolution as resisting Batista's unconstitutional rule.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: First Declaration of Havana (1960) proclaims "the duty of oppressed and exploited nations to fight for their liberation" and the "irrevocable dilemma: Patria or Death!"; in the 1961 May Day speech he says "we prefer to die rather than surrender" the country.

restore-past-order.rationale: The revolution is forward-looking and aims to overthrow the old order.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Second Declaration condemns imperialist exploitation of underdeveloped countries and calls for ending it.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: History Will Absolve Me cites Locke, Rousseau and Althusius for the "right of insurrection against tyranny"; at the 1967 OLAS closing he says the "only one solution" in Latin America is guerrilla warfare and that peaceful power-taking claims "deceiving the masses". The Second Declaration of Havana says "The duty of every revolutionary is to make the revolution", and notes that the bourgeoisie itself once "considered revolution necessary and just".

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: UN speech (1960): "with a fifth of what the world spends on armaments, we could promote the development of all the underdeveloped countries", and aid to Latin America must be "planned and granted unconditionally"; My Life, ch. 14: he proposed a Marshall Plan for Latin America of "about $20 billion" in 1959. In his 1992 Rio speech he adds that the consumer societies' wealth came from colonial and imperialist policies and that the poor must not be asked to forgo development.

separate-church-state.rationale: Speech of 1 May 1961, on nationalising the private schools: "Religion is one thing, politics another"; religion can be taught "in the churches", and the churches "can remain open", but they may not "make war on the people". He does not discuss the state's legal relation to religion more broadly.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Second Declaration holds that entrenched ruling classes cannot be removed by legal reform, and the revolution dismantled Batista's army and state.

socialism-needs-revolutionary-war.rationale: OLAS closing speech (1967): socialism cannot "come to power peacefully"; anyone asserting that "are deceiving the masses", and "guerrilla warfare" is the only long-run solution. He treats a bloodless victory in one country as possible only through the blood of a whole continent's revolutionaries.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Fidelismo claims to be rule by the working people through the revolutionary vanguard, and Castro's Second Declaration frames the revolution as the workers' and peasants' own.

socialized-care.rationale: Speech to the Congress of Women of the Americans (1963): the revolution works to build "children's centers, student dining halls" and laundries so that women are "not to be a slave of the kitchen", to free women "from domestic slavery".

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Castro's 1953 program was a restored constitution, though the revolution held power as a legitimate source.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Castro championed cancelling Third World debt, and the Second Declaration attacks imperialist extraction.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: he calls the Soviet Union "the world's first socialist state" and says its figures "demonstrate unequivocally the victory of socialism over capitalism".

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: First Declaration of Havana (1960) proclaims "the right of nations" to "arm their workers, their peasants, their students" so that they may "themselves defend their rights"; it speaks of nations arming their peoples, not of private persons' weapons as such.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Castro cited Lenin's State and Revolution on destroying the old state machine.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: socialism "will never tolerate crime, never tolerate torture" and its rule "does not mean torture, murder, crime", which he assigns to the dictatorship of the bourgeoisie.

troops-home-from-abroad.rationale: UN speech (1960): foreign bases are a "limitation on sovereignty", "each base is a dagger thrust into sovereignty"; he demands that the United States stop curtailing other nations' sovereignty to keep them. He aims this at bases kept against the host's will.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are celebrated as a revolutionary base, but unions work inside the party-led system rather than as independent bargainers.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Fidelismo's Marxist-Leninist socialism holds that concentrated private wealth enables ruling-class domination; the 1953 programme and later nationalisations aimed to end it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Speech to the Congress of Women of the Americans (1963): "there cannot be rights of women in our America or rights of children, mothers, or wives if there is no revolution"; women are "exploited as a worker and discriminated against as a woman" under the old order.

worker-farmer-alliance.rationale: Second Declaration of Havana (1962): the peasants are the class of of decisive importance in the struggle for national liberation and need "the revolutionary and political leadership of the working class"; he calls for one liberation movement uniting workers and peasants.

workers-anti-imperialist-capitalist-alli.rationale: Second Declaration of Havana (1962): the anti-imperialist struggle can unite the working class, peasants, intellectuals, petty bourgeoisie and "the most progressive layers of the national bourgeoisie", with "a place for all progressives"; he adds that the national bourgeoisie cannot lead that struggle.

workers-nation.rationale: My Life, ch. 3 (Entering Politics): "Chauvinism is the bane of sincere internationalism, and without internationalism there is no salvation for humanity", adding that the Revolution "benefited from the saving kindnesses of internationalism" and suffered from chauvinism.

workers-own-party.rationale: Speech of 2 Dec 1961: he is organising "a strong, disciplined and firm vanguard political organization of the working class", a selective party unlike the traditional ones that "opened the doors wide".

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Second Declaration describes exploitation of Latin America by imperialism, exporting raw materials and importing manufactures.

missingStatements.text: Latin American revolutionaries should unite against foreign domination of the continent.
missingStatements.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana calls the peoples of Latin America to one common anti-imperialist struggle, saying "No nation in Latin America is weak" because each is part of one family of peoples with the same enemy.

keyFigures.role: Leader of the Cuban Revolution and namesake of Castroism

evidence.quote: Only gradually did Castroism come to identify itself with Marxism-Leninism, although from the very beginning of the Cuban revolution Castro revealed his attachment to certain of Marx’s ideas.

A better way to understand Castroism is as a system that sought to combine the economic and political elements of Marxism with those of Simón Bolívar , whose anti-imperialist bent is clearly evident in Castro’s own philosophy.

scope: Castroism (Fidelismo) as the theory and practice associated with Fidel Castro and the Cuban Revolution: in 1953 a nationalism stressing democracy and social justice (History Will Absolve Me), by 1961-62 an avowed Marxism-Leninism that Britannica reads as Marxism combined with Bolívar's anti-imperialism, and in power a one-party, institutionalised state with social welfare, mass mobilisation, charismatic leadership and support for revolutions abroad (Oxford). It includes the armed popular revolution and the guerrilla as revolutionary war (Gran Enciclopèdia Catalana). Answers rest on the reference works that define it and on Castro's own texts: his speeches and declarations of 1953-1992 and the interview book My Life. It excludes Guevara's, Debray's and other Latin American Marxisms except where Castro himself states the position, and it excludes later Cuban government policy that Castro's texts do not state.
